fixes.explanation: Hills are a stretch, friend. This monster is a thing of the seas, and the lament says he thrashes about "…in your rivers…" (Ezekiel 32:2). Mountains show up later in the passage, but they're not where he splashes. Stay near the water on this one.

Right, baker. Pharaoh doesn't keep anything clear. The lament says he is "…churning up the waters with your feet and muddying the streams." (Ezekiel 32:2). I've made a mess on my own counter before, so I won't judge.
Yes, baker. God says, "I will abandon you on the land and hurl you into the open field." (Ezekiel 32:4). The net draws him up out of the water, and he ends up on the land.

Going back to the water is a natural guess, friend. But God says the opposite: "I will abandon you on the land and hurl you into the open field." (Ezekiel 32:4). The net draws him up, and the land and the open field are where he's left.
A well is a creative guess, friend. But the text says, "I will abandon you on the land and hurl you into the open field." (Ezekiel 32:4). The place named is an open field.

Not this time, baker. It's way bigger than one small spot. God says, "I will put your flesh on the mountains and fill the valleys with your remains." (Ezekiel 32:5). Mountains and valleys are a lot of ground.

Right, baker. It isn't one small spot at all. God says, "I will put your flesh on the mountains and fill the valleys with your remains." (Ezekiel 32:5). Mountains and valleys cover a whole lot of ground.

Falling is a dramatic guess, friend, but it isn't what the text says. The sun gets covered with a cloud, the moon "…will not give its light." and the stars are darkened (Ezekiel 32:7). Darkened is the word, not fallen.

You got it, baker. God says, "…their kings will shudder in horror because of you when I brandish My sword before them." (Ezekiel 32:10). Pharaoh's fall shakes up many peoples and their kings. When something that big drops, a lot of folks feel it.
Rescue isn't what the verse says, friend. God says the kings "…will shudder in horror because of you when I brandish My sword before them." (Ezekiel 32:10). Their reaction is horror.
That's the word, baker. God says, "Then I will let her waters settle and will make her rivers flow like oil…" (Ezekiel 32:14). The waters settle, and the rivers flow like oil.
Rising isn't the word, friend. God says, "Then I will let her waters settle and will make her rivers flow like oil…" (Ezekiel 32:14). Settle is the word the verse uses.
Boiling isn't the word, baker. God says, "Then I will let her waters settle…" (Ezekiel 32:14). He also says He will make her rivers flow like oil.
That's right, baker. God says, "…then they will know that I am the LORD." (Ezekiel 32:15). What comes to be known is who He is.
Not in this verse, friend. God says Egypt becomes a desolation and then "…they will know that I am the LORD." (Ezekiel 32:15). What comes to be known there is who He is.

True, baker. God says, "This is the lament they will chant for her; the daughters of the nations will chant it." (Ezekiel 32:16). The daughters of the nations are the ones who chant it. A lament that big needs a big choir.
